 This appeal coming on for orders this day, the court passed
the following:
 Order

This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by appellant/Insurance Company under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'MV Act, 1988') by being aggrieved by award dated 12.03.2021 passed in Claim Case No.65/2018 passed by Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Sonkutch, District-Dewas (MP).

entities.text:
Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Sonkutch
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: (2) Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in the instant case the accident has occurred in the premises of M/s. Kriti Soya Factory and, therefore, the above place does not comes within the purview of 'Public Place'.

Hence, in view of Section 146 and 147 of Motor Vehicles Act, compensation cannot be awarded and prays that this appeal be allowed and Insurance Company be exonerated from liability to pay the compensation.

(3) Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/claimant has placed reliance upon the judgment of High Court of Andhra Pradesh in the case of Pinnaboyina Chittamma and Others vs. B.
Narasingarao and Others dated 20.06.2002 reported in 2002 (6) ALT 723 and submits that the place of accident comes within the purview of 'Public Place'.

entities.text:
Pinnaboyina Chittamma and Others vs. B.
Narasingarao and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence prays that this appeal be dismissed on this ground only.
(4) I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have perused the records of Courts below.

(5) I have gone through paras 21 to 28 of impugned award and therein learned Tribunal, after relying on various judgments of this Court as well as other High Courts, and has concluded that the place of accident is a 'public place' and has negated the contentions of appellant/Insurance Company.

In the instant case, place of accident is premises of M/s. Kriti Soya Factory and certainly it is public place for the purposes of compensation in relation to motor vehicle accident under Motor Vehicles Act.
(6) I do not find any illegality or perversity in the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal, on above points.

(7) So far as amount of compensation is concerned, in this case, the accident has occurred on 01.02.2017 and Tribunal has determined the deceased's monthly income as Rs.6000/- per month,
which cannot be said to be excessive or on higher side.
It is also established from evidence on record that deceased was working as Cleaner at the time of accident.
Hence, it cannot be said that Claims Tribunal has awarded excessive compensation.
